content.text: {"persuasion":"PERSUADED","support_scope":"FULL","rationale":"The book's core identification — love as self-giving covenant allegiance that, for creatures under God's authority, is embodied in commandment-keeping — is stated in the cited texts using Scripture's own definitional formulas: 'this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments' (1 John 5:3), 'this is love, that we walk after his commandments' (2 John 6), 'If ye love me, keep my commandments' (John 14:15), and the Deuteronomic pairing of loving the LORD with keeping His commandments (Deut 10:12-13; Ex 20:6). The strongest counter — mainstream agape as a self-giving benevolent disposition of which obedience is fruit rather than constitution — must soften those definitional formulas into merely evidential statements ('love is shown by keeping'), an interpretive step the texts themselves do not supply. Meanwhile the book already answers the counter's two best proof points: 1 Cor 13:3 (deeds without love profit nothing) is used by the book itself to deny behaviorist reduction — the allegiance, not the bare deed, is the substance — and 1 John 4:8-10 (God is love; God obeys no superior) is handled by the explicit qualifier 'for those under God's authority,' locating the common center in self-giving allegiance rather than in obedience per se. Romans 13:10 ('love is the fulfilling of the law') further binds love to the commandments rather than to a free-floating disposition. Accepted prior premises on Belief and Faith establish the same covenantal grammar (obedience constitutive of the covenant response, not merely downstream), and the love texts fit that grammar at least as tightly. No supplied text is better explained by the counter than by the book's core.","book_core_identification":"Love is self-giving covenant allegiance; for those under God's authority, that allegiance is constitutively embodied in keeping His commandments — such that obedience severed from allegiance is empty sacrifice (1 Cor 13:3), and professed love that persistently refuses His commands is a false profession (1 John 5:3; John 14:15; 2 John 6).","book_secondary_elaborations":["The two great commandments as two tables: the first four commandments as how one loves God, the last six as how one loves neighbor","1 Corinthians 13 read as a legal audit itemizing the law (envy = tenth commandment; 'rejoices in the truth' = the law per Ps 119:142), converging with Matthew 7:22-23 and 1 Samuel 15:22","Hate defined as the opposite pole of the same axis — covenant un-choosing rather than emotional heat (Gen 29:30-31; Luke 14:26 // Matt 10:37; Hos 9:15; Ex 20:5-6)","The 'mirror' of 1 Cor 13:12 identified with the law via James 1:23-25, and 'face to face' with Num 12:8","The claim that 'love never ends' because the law it fulfills does not pass away","Lexical claims about satam vs. sane underlying the KJV's 'hated'"],"strongest_counter_interpretation":"The mainstream agape reading: love primarily names God's own self-giving, sacrificial, benevolent nature supremely revealed in Christ's atoning death (1 John 4:8-10; John 3:16; Rom 5:8), and derivatively the supreme virtue and disposition believers are to have (1 Cor 13). On this reading commandment-keeping is the necessary fruit, evidence, or expression of love, but love itself is identified as the benevolent self-giving disposition, not as covenant allegiance constituted by the keeping; John 14:15 and 1 John 5:3 are read as tests or manifestations of a prior inner reality.","counter_core_identification":"Love is God's own self-giving benevolent nature and the corresponding inner disposition of sacrificial goodwill toward God and neighbor; obedience flows from it as consequence and evidence but is not constitutive of what love is.","counter_relation_to_book_core":"SAME_CORE_BROADER","material_core_denial":"The counter denies that commandment-keeping is constitutive of creaturely love toward God, demoting the definitional statements of 1 John 5:3, 2 John 6, and John 14:15 to descriptions of love's effects, and identifying love instead as a disposition that could in principle be specified without reference to the commanded body it takes.","counter_case":["1 John 4:8-10 grounds love in God's nature and initiative ('not that we loved God, but that he loved us'), suggesting love is prior to and deeper than any command-response","1 Corinthians 13:3 shows that maximal outward performance without love is nothing, indicating love is an inner reality distinct from deeds, including obedient deeds","John 3:16 and
